page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Face-to-face
title: Face-to-face
description:
Anna and the rest of the Tip Top Trading team are at the International Plastics Convention and looking to promote their business. Will Anna be able to network and make some useful contacts at the conference?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use when you are trying to make new business contacts at a conference.
phrases: Excuse me, hello, I'm Anna. I work as a Sales Executive at Tip Top Trading.
Can you tell me about your company?
Can I briefly tell you about what our company does?
I think we might be able to help you.
Here's my business card should you want to call.

listening_challenge.question: What is the name of the company that Jane (the woman that Anna networks with) works for?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. It's the big day of the International Plastics Conference and a good opportunity for the staff at Tip Top Trading to promote its business. But hold on, who's this? It's Mr Socrates, the big boss from America.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Hey, you guys, where have you been?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah, Mr Socrates… nice to see you again. I'd heard you were in town.

transcript.speaker: Anna/Tom
transcript.text: Hello Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: I've been looking for you everywhere. I need to catch up with you and see how business is going.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh very, very well. We're selling Imperial Lemons to France and Anna is developing plastic vegetables.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Ah Anna! My favourite girl. Still doing a good job?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm doing my best.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: In fact she's been doing my job for a few days… had a bit of a biscuit accident…

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Yeah, well that's not hard for you, Paul. Listen, listen I need to talk you - shouldn't the others be doing some networking now?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Of course, that's why we’re here. Right, Tom, I need you to catch up with some of our existing customers – do some schmoozing – and Anna, could you talk to some potential new customers? I need to speak to Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. Erm, networking… what exactly am I supposed to do?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Networking is about helping your business through connecting with other people in the industry. It involves meeting people and talking to them, sharing information, hopefully helping each other and ultimately, getting new business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So I have to talk to strangers?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, yes. Introduce yourself, say who you work for. Ask them about their business and what they do. Then explain a bit about what you do and who uses your products. If it's appropriate, say that you may be able to help them. Then see if they would consider buying from you. Just be chatty and friendly.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. I'll give it a try. Excuse me, hello, I'm Anna. I work as a Sales Executive at Tip Top Trading… and you are?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Jane. Jane from Nice'n'Cheesy. It's very busy here today isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It is. It's my first time here but it's very exciting. I really didn't know what to wear.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna! That's chatty and friendly, but let's get down to business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh yes, of course. So can you tell me about your company, Nice'n'Cheesy?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Well, we sell cheese to London's top cheese shops - we like to say we're a wedge above the rest – a wedge of cheese, get it?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, right. Well, can I briefly tell you about what our company does? Our company – Tip Top Trading – makes plastic fruit mainly for the catering and food industry. We're up for an award today for one of our designs.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Smashing. That's quite interesting actually. We have an issue with the fresh grapes we provide with our cheeses – they keep going mouldy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: Yes – sour grapes you could say! A good quality plastic grape would be useful to put with our cheese displays.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I think we might be able to help you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes you can! This is the time to exchange contact details – give her your business card.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, if I could have your contact details I'll send you one of our brochures and then give you a call about prices.  And here's my business card should you want to call me.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: That's fantastic. So nice to have met you – and I think what you're wearing for the conference is perfect.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Bingo! Looks like Anna has a potential new customer. She was friendly and chatty but kept her mind on business. She used phrases like these:
Excuse me, hello, I'm Anna. I work as a Sales Executive at Tip Top Trading.
Can you tell me about your company?
Can I briefly tell you about what our company does?
I think we might be able to help you.
Here's my business card should you want to call.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So, some good work by Anna but there's more networking to be done. A conference is a good place for networking and for catching up with your boss, too. Let's find out how Paul is getting on with Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: It's a tough economic climate Paul. We're already cutting out cookies in management meetings.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh, gosh.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: And now we're cutting staff. We've already lost Rachel – my favourite Sales Executive.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah yes, well, she was stealing the pens.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Pens can be replaced but not people like her.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well…

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: But now it's time to reduce your team Paul – share the pain.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Are you sure?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Absolutely. By my calculations you need to be rid of one member of staff.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh… well let's not tell the team until we've had the awards ceremony.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: OK Paul. But it's in your hands to sort this out.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Crumbs!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ah yes, Tip Top Trading could be about to win a prestigious award but how will this bad news go down with the team? And what is Paul going to do? Find out next time on English at Work.
